transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The U.S. military says it's disabled a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman
as it attempted to break the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports.
The strike comes as the Trump administration has been noncommittal
on its next move nine months into the U.S. war in Iran.
NPR's Kat Lanzdorf has more.
U.S. Central Command says a military aircraft fired "precision munitions"
at a merchant vessel attempting to leave an Iranian port.
CENTCOM said in a statement that the civilian crew of the ship was unharmed.
The U.S. military has been blocking Iranian ports since April.
It temporarily lifted the blockade over the summer during talks with Tehran
but resumed it in July.
This strike was the 15th ship the U.S. has disclosed disabling during its blockade,
including at least two strikes that have resulted in the killing of multiple crew members.
President Trump has wavered on what to do next in Iran,
suggesting on Thanksgiving Day that the end of the war will be "whenever he decides."
Kat Lanzdorf, NPR News, Washington.
Senate Democrats are set to hold leadership elections next week
where the race for majority leader is contested.
NPR's Elena Moore reports lawmakers are deciding between
Chuck Schumer of New York and Chris Van Hollen of Maryland.
Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change in Washington
when they retake a majority next year,
but they're split over who should lead that shift.
Schumer, who's been the top Democrat in the Senate since 2017,
says he has enough votes to win.
Van Hollen calls himself an underdog and says he's running on more of a populist message,
hoping to capitalize on broader dissatisfaction voters have with the party establishment.
However, unlike the midterms, this isn't an election decided by voters.
It'll come down to other senators from their own party
and will be decided by secret ballot.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
Stocks sharply higher this holiday-shortened week.
The gains were welcomed by investors who have spent the past several days worrying about AI.
NPR's Muhammed Javed has more.
After several days of volatile fluctuations, mostly due to tech indexes,
U.S. stocks posted strong returns this week before the market closed today.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.6 percent with broad gains.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2 percent.
And the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 2.3 percent.
The biggest jump this week was on Monday when Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia,
was reinstated as the head of the semiconductor company.
Those gains have held despite big ups and downs on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Semiconductor stocks bounced back as investors relaxed about instability in the AI market.
The market was shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday and closed early for Black Friday.
Muhammed Javed, NPR News.
And Wall Street closed today at 1 p.m.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Budget airline North Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy protection
a day after stopping flights and ticket sales.
The Norwegian airline was founded in 2021
and offered cheap flights from Europe to Asia, South Africa and the United States.
This comes nearly seven months after U.S. budget carrier Spirit Airlines filed for bankruptcy
and then went out of business.
North says despite extensive efforts, it wasn't able to find sufficient funding to continue.
Higher jet fuel prices from the U.S. war in Iran put significant stress on smaller airlines
that weren't in good financial shape at the start of the year.
There are big crowds at the movie theaters this weekend.
As NPR's Bob Mondello reports, Hollywood is optimistic about an end-of-the-year box office bonanza.
With a Hunger Games sequel...
Twice the number of triggers, twice the glory.
Helping to push this weekend's ticket sales above $200 million,
movie theater owners are turning their attention to next month
and what's likely to be the biggest sequel-driven opening day in Hollywood history.
December 18, when the conclusion of Denis Villeneuve's Dune trilogy...
Opens on the same day as Marvel's superhero epic Avengers Doomsday.
I am Dune.
Fans are calling the blockbuster battle Dune's Day,
and they've already ponied up tens of millions of dollars for advance tickets to both films.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: U.S. military disables a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman attempting to break the Iranian port blockade
Senate Democrats set to hold leadership elections pitting Chuck Schumer against Chris Van Hollen for majority leader
U.S. stocks rise sharply in holiday-shortened week, led by tech gains after Jensen Huang reinstated at Nvidia
Norwegian budget airline North Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy after halting flights and ticket sales
Movie theaters see strong weekend ticket sales, with Hunger Games sequel and December Dune and Avengers releases ahead
